newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate edges up amid higher demand.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate edges up amid higher demand.

text.p: The average lending rate edged up 20 basis points to 9.6 percent on Monday as demand for fresh loans rose in brisker trade on Croatia's interbank market.
Total settlements doubled to 62 million kuna, of which most were new kuna funds, but demand at 92 million could not be completely satisfied. Supply was higher at 105 million kuna.
Demand for interbank 10-15 and 15-30 day loans was met at 9.1 and 9.5 percent respectively. A smaller three-month loan was made at 15.5 percent.
Call money was unchanged at 8.0 percent while one-week funds were rolled over at 12 percent. Insurers' short-term rate was steady at 7.0 percent.
Overnight trade over the weekend totalled 119.2 million kuna as five banks with shortfalls squared their positions.

The central bank stayed out of the hard currency market on Monday. Its kuna mid-rates for Tuesday eased to 5.3993 from 5.3867 to the dollar and to 3.5599 from 3.5537 against the mark. -- Laura Lui, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
